title: Polynomial-time closure for the bad-specification language
statement: Let $C,c	ext{ in } acks lash	extbackslash N$, and let $V$ be a language of bit strings in $P$. Form the language of strings $z$ for which the five decoded components $x,U,u,j,p$ satisfy the following: $|u|=C(|x|+1)^c$, $|j|\le C(|x|+1)^c$, and $|p|\le C(|x|+1)^c$; and at least one of the following holds. The circuit encoded by the marker-deleted $U$, queried on $ g x,u g$ with the all-ones marker of length $C(|x|+1)^c$ followed by $0$, rejects; or $|p|=C(|x|+1)^c$, that circuit accepts the query with suffix $0p$, and $ g g x,p g$ is not in $V$; or $|j|+|p|+1=C(|x|+1)^c$, the circuit accepts the query with suffix $1 0 p$ preceded by $|j|$ ones, and rejects both queries with suffixes $0(p0)$ and $0(p1)$ preceded by $|j|$ ones. Then this language is in $P$.
caveat: The statement depends on nested pair decoding and circuit-query encodings, which are rendered descriptively.
